problem_text:
A logistics firm is tasked with orchestrating a synchronized inspection tour across five regional warehouses, each situated at distinct geographical points:
Warehouse Alpha: Positioned at grid reference (115,126)
Warehouse Beta: Positioned at grid reference (169,164)
Warehouse Gamma: Positioned at grid reference (179,91)
Warehouse Delta: Positioned at grid reference (21,83)
Warehouse Epsilon: Positioned at grid reference (156,29)

The travel distances between these facilities, measured along available transport corridors, are precisely known:
Alpha to Gamma: 72.9 km
Alpha to Delta: 103.4 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 105.3 km
Beta to Gamma: 73.7 km
Beta to Delta: 168.7 km
Beta to Epsilon: 135.6 km
Gamma to Delta: 158.2 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 66.1 km
Delta to Epsilon: 145.4 km

Due to infrastructural limitations, no direct corridor exists connecting Warehouse Alpha and Warehouse Beta.
Furthermore, operational protocols mandate that the final route must incorporate exactly one of two critical, but mutually exclusive, supply links: either the corridor between Warehouse Beta and Warehouse Gamma, or the corridor between Warehouse Gamma and Warehouse Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient cyclical inspection circuit, commencing and concluding at the same warehouse, while ensuring each facility is visited precisely once.
